summary: AE+SE run through POC milestones: kickoff, access and sample data, benchmark sprint (latency & cost), mid-point review, exec readout. Customer emphasized need for VPC isolation, p95 latency < 400ms for generation use-case, and cost target under their internal $0.0009/token equivalent. Agreement to run two benchmark sweeps (light and heavy) and one midpoint functional QA. Action items captured.
topics: Workload sizing: TPS and token distribution
Midpoint review criteria and exec readout
transcript:
[00:00] Lina Morales: Okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. we will run about an hour. quick intros — from redwood i have Devon the SE and Maya on CSM.
[00:12] Arjun Patel: hi all, Arjun here — we do the platform for Kappa Ventures portfolio, we wanted to scope a short POC to validate latency/cost for our assistant flows.
[00:21] Lina Morales: Awesome, high level today is to lock down timeline, what access you can give us, and what success looks like. if that all sounds right we'll table a benchmark cadence.
[00:30] Sofia Romero: yes that matches. just to be explicit, we need VPC peering or private endpoints — cannot send logs to public buckets.
[00:40] Devon Park: noted — we support VPC private control plane for the Private offering, and for hosted we can do VPC endpoints + customer-managed keys. will note that some of our perf numbers change slightly with strict network egress.
[00:52] Evan Liu: Quick question on success criteria: we want p95 generation latency under 400ms for 512 token prompts, and cost per 1k tokens under $0.9 — is that realistic?
[01:05] Devon Park: ok so two parts: latency and cost. with a ded-optimized instance and continuous batching we can hit p50 ~ 120ms and p95 depends on batch window and prefix caching. 400ms p95 for 512 is in the realm but depends on tokenization and concurrency.
[01:28] Arjun Patel: our load profile is spiky — peak concurrency 120 rps, sustained 40 rps, median tokens per request 350. we'll upload a 24h sample.
[01:38] Lina Morales: perfect, that helps. we'll size the benchmark nodes for 120rps peak and run two sweeps: a light-run for functional correctness and a heavy-run for sustained throughput.
[01:50] Sofia Romero: can you also run a quantized variant? we need to see cost/latency tradeoffs and any quality diffs.
[01:58] Devon Park: yes, we'll include a quantized 4-bit run and a float16 run. note: sometimes token generation speed changes nonlinearly with quantization; we'll capture perplexity drift and a small eval set.
[02:12] Evan Liu: how long will the benchmark sprint take?
[02:16] Lina Morales: recommended plan: kickoff this week (access gating + data), benchmark sprint week 2 (two full sweeps across model variants), midpoint review end of week 3, and exec readout week 4. so roughly a 3-week active window plus prep.
[02:33] Arjun Patel: timeline okay but our security review needs to sign off before any sample data leaves VPC. how do you handle that?
[02:40] Maya Chen: we typically provide an on-prem ingestion option or encrypted SFTP to your VPC, and we can run the initial bench in your VPC for Private customers. we'll also share SOC2 docs and architecture diagrams.
[02:55] Sofia Romero: can you send the runbook and the checklist? we need to map to our internal SR process.
[03:01] Lina Morales: yes — action item: we'll send the benchmark spreadsheet, access checklist, and SOC2 link after the call.
[03:09] Devon Park: technical note: we'll need a representative prompt set and expected tokenization. also want to confirm whether you use streaming responses or chunked generation — streaming can change latency profile.
[03:22] Arjun Patel: primary flows are streaming chat with function-calls for lookups, so we expect many small messages and occasional long responses.
[03:30] Devon Park: ok stream heavy. we'll run both streaming and non-streaming to capture real-world. also will instrument KV cache hit-rate — prefix caching can reduce cost significantly if you have repeated contexts.
[03:44] Evan Liu: regarding benchmarks, what metrics will you report?
[03:47] Devon Park: we'll report p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, throughput, unit cost per 1k tokens, GPU utilization, and a simple quality delta on your eval prompts. we'll include logs and a short Ops runbook.
[04:02] Arjun Patel: about model variants — we prefer an open family, nothing proprietary, and we want ability to fallback to a smaller cheaper variant if load spikes.
[04:12] Lina Morales: that's standard, we'll propose a primary model and a compact fallback, plus a quantized option. routing policies and automatic fallback are part of the Dedicated setup.
[04:25] Sofia Romero: curious about observability retention — our legal needs 1 year of audit logs.
[04:31] Maya Chen: we can retain token-level traces for that window on Dedicated or Private with enterprise retention add-on; we will surface cost buckets at token granularity in Console.
[04:44] Evan Liu: any blockers from your side to start?
[04:47] Arjun Patel: main blocker is legal sign-off on the access path. once we confirm SFTP or VPC peering, we can give sample traces.
[04:56] Lina Morales: action items recap: we send runbook + spreadsheet; Kappa uploads sample traffic; Devon prepares quantized config. we'll tentatively book midpoint review for 2026-09-23.
[05:08] Sofia Romero: can we include an early smoke test within 48 hours of access? we'd like a quick sanity run.
[05:15] Devon Park: yes, we'll do a 2-hour smoke test as soon as credentials are in place — sanity checks on latency, correctness, and access controls.
[05:24] Arjun Patel: one more on cost math — your per-token math sometimes uses different tokenization base, can you include exact tokenization library and sample token counts?
[05:32] Devon Park: we'll include the tokenizer version and a tokenization sample for your prompts.
[05:37] Lina Morales: great, any other Qs?
[05:40] Evan Liu: competitors: we ran a quick check with Vertex and Triton setups, but wanted to see Redwood's ability to route and fallback efficiently.
[05:49] Devon Park: routing is policy driven — region/cost/latency based. during benchmark we'll exercise fallback to cheaper model if latency thresholds breach.
[05:58] Arjun Patel: thanks all. next steps and owners are in the notes, and we'll follow up by email.
[06:06] Lina Morales: thanks everyone — we'll send materials today and lock the kickoff once sample data path is confirmed.
[06:12] Meeting ended.
notes: Customer requires VPC/private ingestion, p95 < 400ms for 512 tokens target, peak 120 rps, plan for two benchmark sweeps and a midpoint review. Security and legal sign-off gating access. Quantized & float variants to be bench-marked. Smoke test within 48h post access.
